meta.title: Accessibility
meta.description: The target, what every change is tested against, the gaps that remain, and where to report one.

target.intro: The target is WCAG 2.2 level AA for the component and for this site. That is a target the tests enforce, not a certification: no audit has been commissioned, and no conformance claim is made.
points: The default preset meets the contrast requirements in both color schemes.
Everything that can be done with a pointer can be done with a keyboard, in the order the page reads.
Every part carries a role and a name; nothing depends on color alone.
Under prefers-reduced-motion nothing animates, and no information is carried by motion.

tested.intro: Every change runs the same checks, and a release adds the ones a person has to do:
points: axe-core over the rendered component in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, in both presets, both color schemes and every state, with the contrast rules on.
axe-core over the pages of this site, in each locale, with no serious or critical violation allowed.
Keyboard tests that walk the whole schedule: the cards, the pinned chips, the navigation, the dialogs and the way focus returns.
Snapshots of what a screen reader is given — the accessible names, the live-region announcements and their throttling.
Right-to-left screenshots against their left-to-right counterparts, so a mirrored layout is a test failure rather than a surprise.
Before a release, the manual checklist: NVDA with Firefox and VoiceOver with Safari, keyboard-only demo tasks, 200% zoom at 320 pixels wide, and Windows High Contrast.

gaps.intro: The gaps that are known, and what is being done about them:
points: There is no roving focus between cards yet: <kbd>Tab</kbd> is the only movement, and a shift with many items is many stops. It is on the <link to="/discover-more/roadmap/">roadmap</link>.
The navigation buttons have no keyboard shortcuts.

The classic preset keeps a few contrast shortfalls on purpose, for pixel parity with the look it reproduces: the level pills, the alert tint, and three more in the light scheme. The default preset has none, and the test suite allows exactly that list and nothing else.

One color of this documentation site — the border of inputs and hovered cards — is below the 3:1 that its own design system claims. It is measured in a test so it cannot get worse, and it belongs to the shell rather than to the component.
The manual checklist has not run yet, because nothing has been released yet.

reporting.intro: An accessibility issue is a bug, and it is triaged ahead of features. When reporting one:
points: Say which assistive technology and browser, with versions — the combination matters more than either on its own.
Say what you expected to hear or reach, and what happened instead.
A link to a reproduction is worth more than a description; the <link to="/demos/">demos</link> are a fair starting point.
<link to="/getting-started/support/">Support</link> has the place to open it and what else to include.
